tools.name: get_workspace
tools.description: The workspace this key belongs to: its id, name and plan, and this period's usage.

tools.name: get_usage
tools.description: Plan, runs used this billing period, included runs, extra-run packng period, included runs, extra-run packs and runs left. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

tools.name: get_network
tools.description: How our browsers reach your sites: the static addresses to allow-list, the country they browse from, and the countries available. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

tools.name: set_browse_from
tools.description: Choose the country our browsers and devices reach your sites and app servers from (web and app tests), or automatic: the site's own country (an app test then uses our default country). Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: The projects in this workspace (a project groups the tests of one site or app). Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

tools.name: get_project
tools.description: One project. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

tools.name: create_project
tools.description: Create a project, for example one per site or app. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

tools.name: update_project
tools.description: Rename a project or change its description. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

tools.name: delete_project
tools.description: Archive a project: its tests stop running; past runs stay in the run history. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

tools.name: list_tests
tools.description: The tests of a project, each with its latest run. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

tools.name: get_test
tools.description: One test: its start address, requirement, plan, options and latest run. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

tools.name: create_test

tools.name: delete_test
tools.description: Archive a test: it stops running; past runs stay in the run history. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

tools.description: Files a test can upload during its steps (for example an import file). Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

tools.name: add_test_file
tools.description: Add a file the tester can upload during the test: up to 25 MB, up to 10 files per test. tools.name: delete_test_file

tools.description: The sign-in accounts stored for a project: names, usernames and sites. Passwords are never returned. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

tools.description: Save the definition of one call into your own system that the tester may make during a run (for example "create a voucher"). tools.name: delete_endpoint
tools.description: Delete an endpoint. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

tools.name: list_runs
tools.description: Recent runs, newest first, optionally for one test or project or with one status; or the runs with the given ids. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

tools.name: get_run
tools.description: A run: its status, and once final the verdict, the headline, each check's result with the reason, the values read, and links to the video, screenshots and the result page. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

tools.name: wait_run

tools.name: stop_run
tools.description: Stop a queued or running run. A run you stop is not counted. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

tools.name: create_watch_link
tools.description: A view-only link to watch a run live and read its result, with no sign-in, valid while it runs and for some hours after. tools.name: revoke_watch_link
tools.description: Turn off every watch link of a run straight away. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

tools.name: list_share_links
tools.description: The share links made for a run, with when they expire and how often they were opened. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

tools.name: create_share_link
tools.description: A read-only link to a run's result, replay and video that anyone can open without signing in, until it expires. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

tools.name: delete_share_link
tools.description: Turn off a share link straight away. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

tools.name: list_schedules
tools.description: When tests run by themselves: every schedule in the workspace, or those of one test or project. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

tools.name: create_schedule
tools.description: Run a test by itself: on chosen weekdays, or monthly on a day, at a time in a time zone. Each scheduled run counts like any other run. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

tools.name: update_schedule
tools.description: Pause or resume a schedule. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

tools.name: delete_schedule
tools.description: Delete a schedule. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

tools.name: list_devices
tools.description: The phones and tablets app tests can run on, and their OS versions (latest first). Pass device and osVersion to create_test, update_test, run_test or run_project. findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: plan_test, create_build_upload · Private data: create_test, duplicate_test, plan_test, list_test_files, add_test_file, delete_test_file, list_credentials, add_credential, delete_credential, find_build, create_build_upload, import_build, complete_build_upload · Public sink: list_test_files, add_test_file, run_test, run_project, list_share_links, create_share_link, delete_share_link, create_build_upload, import_build, complete_build_upload · Destructive: get_usage, delete_project, list_tests, get_test, create_test, duplicate_test, delete_test, delete_test_file, delete_credential, list_endpoints, add_endpoint, delete_endpoint, run_test, run_project, get_run, wait_run, stop_run, create_watch_link, revoke_watch_link, list_share_links, create_share_link, delete_share_link, list_schedules, create_schedule, delete_schedule, list_devices, find_build, create_build_upload, import_build, complete_build_upload, delete_build.

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
